research_scope: Source-free whole-formulation-anchored review of shared prerequisite identities; no source/definition mutation, no parent-definition equivalence, no freeze or gate change.

aliases.reason: Both original statements use the same finite-rank free R-module R^n: the finite projective module source states M is a direct summand of R^n; the finitely presented and Lazard sources use finite free modules. Their common prerequisite is the standard finite direct sum R⊕⋯⊕R with n≥0; projectivity, presentation and flatness are conditions on their separate parent statements.

The abelian category statement calls its canonical Coim(f)→Im(f) arrow an isomorphism; the groupoid statement defines an isomorphism by a two-sided inverse g with gf=id and fg=id. Both use precisely the general categorical isomorphism notion. The abelian-category hypotheses and source-specific canonical comparison are not assimilated into the prerequisite.

Both subspace-topology variants explicitly form τ_A={A∩U:U∈τ}; the shared prerequisite A∩U is binary set intersection. The general variant allows A=∅ and the alternate source excludes empty subspaces; that parent-space convention remains in the original formulation and is not a property of intersection.

The convergent-real-series source starts with a real sequence (a_n) indexed by n≥0, while the power-series and ordinary-generating-function sources use a real coefficient sequence over the same indices. All require a function ℕ_0→ℝ as the shared prerequisite; convergence or a centered formal series is an extra parent-statement condition.
